name: TX-08
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district (R+13 PVI) in a favorable GOP environment
Republican Steinmann has massive financial edge: $2.1M raised plus $1.7M outside support vs. negligible Democratic fundraising
Open seat removes incumbent advantage but does not change the partisan baseline
Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 95%
model.rationale: The R+13 district, a strong Republican fundraising and outside-spending advantage, and markets pricing the GOP near 95% all point the same direction, with no polls or ratings suggesting anything different. The Democratic candidate has raised almost nothing, so the race stays firmly in Republican territory.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending on the Democratic side would be the first sign of movement, but nothing currently indicates a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This open Houston-area seat is solidly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about thirteen points toward the GOP and a favorable national environment for Republicans this cycle. Morgan Luttrell's retirement puts a new name on the ballot, but the seat's fundamentals remain unchanged.

Republican Jessica Hart Steinmann has raised over $2 million and benefits from roughly $1.7 million in outside support, while Democrat Laura Jones has raised about $22,000 with no outside help. Prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 95% chance, and no polls or expert ratings suggest the race is competitive. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican win in the mid-teens.
